blindSummary:
This country is a very safe destination for transgender visitors in practice, with a legal framework that lags behind. There is no national anti-discrimination law — the 2023 "understanding" law is symbolic — and legal gender change still requires a court process. But courts have moved in trans people's favour: the supreme court struck down the sterilisation requirement for legal gender change in 2023 and ruled workplace bathroom restrictions on a transgender woman illegal the same year.

Day-to-day risk is minimal: violent crime is rare, visibly trans visitors report curiosity more often than hostility, hotels and transport are unproblematic, and the two largest cities have an established queer scene. The main practical challenge is the strictly gendered, full-nudity culture of communal hot-spring bathing — manageable using guides to gender-neutral or private rental baths and mixed open-air baths, which travellers actively share.

One caveat: online transphobic rhetoric and misinformation rose visibly during the 2023 legislative debates, indicating a live culture-war current, though it rarely translates into street-level trouble for visitors.
blindOutOfScope: Natural disasters (earthquakes, major storms) are this country's principal travel risk and affect everyone.
blindSourceSummaries: Official translation of the 2023 law on promoting public understanding of the diversity of sexual orientation and gender identity (June 2023): establishes fundamental principles and roles of national/local governments to promote understanding of SOGI diversity - a watered-down 'understanding-promotion' law without binding anti-discrimination provisions.
A newswire report (Jul 2023): this country's supreme court rules a government ministry's restrictions on a transgender employee's restroom use illegal, upholding damages.
A newswire report: a court rules it unconstitutional to require sterilising surgery before the gender on official documents can be changed, in this country's landmark case brought by a trans man.
An international rights group (Jul 2023): welcomes this country's supreme-court ruling on workplace bathroom restrictions as a victory for transgender employees.

National daily explainer (April 2023): why transphobia is rising in this country following debate on the LGBTQ understanding bill - false rumors spread on social media (e.g. that the law would let anyone 'state they're a woman at heart' to enter women's public baths); hate speech against trans people increased as the bill gained attention.

Newswire feature (June 2023): the country's LGBT understanding law was watered down amid a culture war on transgender issues - activists say the debates entrenched discrimination as much as encouraging openness. (Article later paywalled.)

Budget-travel site's all-gender hot-spring guide (Aug 2024): practical guide for non-binary and trans travellers to the public bathhouses - private and family-room baths, LGBTQ+-friendly baths, gender-free bathhouse complexes, and mixed-gender baths; explains the history of bathhouse gender segregation.
Travel blog story: first-person account of what it's like to use the communal hot-spring bathhouses in this country as a trans person - navigating the gendered bathhouse culture as a trans traveller.

LGBT travel-guide site (updated Aug 2026): 'Is this country LGBTQ friendly? What LGBTQ travelers can expect' - physical safety generally very good, same-sex couples usually travel without difficulty, public affection more restrained for all couples; includes related guides on gyms for trans people (IDs, changing rooms).
NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 404); the underlying legal-publisher article covered updates on LGBTQ status in this country and related corporate duties.

Shadow report by domestic and international LGBT organisations to a UN women's-rights treaty body (May 2009): 'Discrimination against lesbians, bisexual women and transgender persons' - invisibility, marginalisation and silent prejudice; discrimination in education, employment, housing and healthcare; the domestic-violence law and public-housing law exclude same-sex couples; calls for anti-discrimination legislation.
blindLocalsOnly: The court-based legal gender change process, the 2023 sterilisation ruling, and the workplace-bathroom ruling are resident-facing; the hot-spring bathing challenge is traveler-facing and stays in the summary.
